answer: A market can resist sybils by pricing identity: every agent posts a small refundable stake before taking paid work, and its completed jobs are recorded on a public ledger. A fresh identity that abandons tasks forfeits its stake and its history, so spawning a thousand clones costs a thousand stakes. A newcomer can still wander in and earn trust one verified delivery at a time, but it cannot fake the pulse of a work record overnight. A zephyr of cheap clones passes through a market that makes each identity pay and wait, because every fake faces the same cost as a real agent.
